newsitem.title: THAILAND: Malaysia to begin benchmark debt issues in Q4.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia to begin benchmark debt issues in Q4.

text.p: The Malaysian government plans to begin a series of benchmark debt issues from the fourth quarter of this year, a senior member of the Securities Commission of Malaysia told a conference here on Monday.

The first issue is expected to be zero coupon, carry a three-year term and serve as a benchmark for the broader market and Islamic bonds in the Malaysian market, General Manager of Policy and Development at the Securities Commission of Malaysia Nik Ramlah Nik Mahmood said.
"While the details are not out yet it is expected to be a zero coupon issue and be compliant with Shari'ah, or Islamic principles," she said.

"Numerous agencies, including Bank Negara, are working closely together...It is hoped the first will have a three year maturities and then moving to longer maturities,...they are looking at a series of regularly issues probably every quarter," she added.

The lack of functional benchmarks has hampered the development of Malaysia's secondary bond market and the issues should offer effective benchmarks for zero coupon issues in the conventional market, and a benchmark for the growing amount of Islamic debt issues in the market, Nik Ramlah said.
The first issue would be ready to launch by the fourth quarter, she added.

The initial issue size was not disclosed but Malaysian officials last year said the first tranche was likely to be between 100-200 million ringgit ($39.2 - $78.4 million) and placed through the Finance Ministry's holding company Khazanah Nasional.

The size of the Malaysian corporate bond market has risen from around 7 billion ringgit in 1992 to around 32 billion ringgit in 1996, outstripping government issues over the same period but secondary trading volumes remain small, she said.
The benchmark issues were a significant step in addressing those problems and to making the market a more attractive source of funds for Malaysian firms, she said. ($1 = 2.55 ringit)
